source: 26. How can poisoned or instruction-bearing documents attack a ZXNAME0000XZ system, and why should retrieved text be treated as untrusted data? [Advanced - Security] A ZXNAME0001XZ corpus expands the attack surface because retrieved text is external input. PoisonedRAG demonstrated that injecting malicious documents into a knowledge base can steer answers for targeted queries, and later security benchmarks show broader robustness problems with misleading or adversarial context. Even without an optimized poisoning attack, ordinary documents can contain instruction-like text that conflicts with system policy. Retrieved content should therefore be treated as untrusted data: preserve provenance and trust level, separate instructions from evidence in prompt design, restrict which sources can enter sensitive workflows, scan or validate ingestion where appropriate, enforce tool permissions outside the model, and monitor suspicious retrieval patterns.
